attribution.note: A bullet in Marcus's own list of hype complaints, in his own voice. It quotes no one else.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase. It is rhetorical in tone, but it does assert a historical frequency: promised world-changing AI science rarely materialized. No metric or start date was given.

contract.note: The plain reading (only a small share of promises delivered by the post date, with promises not yet due excluded) is ordinary and fair. 'Rarely', 'world-changing' and the promise population are all undefined, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: The 2024 Nobel press release on AlphaFold2 documents one major AI-enabled scientific success before the post. A single success cannot set the proportion of promises fulfilled.

reviews.rationale: The claim is about how often promises were fulfilled. The packet holds one notable success (AlphaFold) and no representative inventory pairing promises with outcomes. The evidence neither shows that fulfillment was infrequent nor that it was common.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in the body of his post.

semantics.note: Keeps his own scope ('dozens of shots on goal') and the universal words 'invariably' and 'never'. This is a historical observation up to the post date.

contract.note: Reading the claim as recurring qualitative failures plus no broadly reliable generalization under distribution shift is ordinary and not stretched either way. The roster of attempts and the meaning of 'solved' are undefined, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, June 2025: frontier reasoning systems including Claude, Gemini and Grok fail uniformly on ARC-AGI-2, suggesting shared limits. It covers one benchmark, not dozens of attempts or controlled distribution shifts.
The pre-post version of the ASU paper uses a tiny GPT-2-style model. It does not test the named frontier families.
A small citation test in which Grok and DeepSeek fabricated no references. This narrowly qualifies a uniform reading of the failures. It says nothing about distribution shift.

reviews.rationale: The ARC evidence supports shared limits across the named families. The packet has no comprehensive evaluation of dozens of attempts and no controlled distribution-shift tests on frontier models. It also shows no validated solution to distribution shift, so neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence, which plays on the Transformer paper's title.

semantics.note: The sentence is phrased as a present finding ('it turns out'), but in context it claims a limit on reaching AGI. Reading it as an undated firm forecast that attention-based scaling alone won't reach AGI is defensible. Adding 'to get to AGI' follows from the context.

contract.note: The reading covers attention-based LLMs with their usual components and an AGI meaning broadly human-level. That is ordinary. Because no deadline exists, early resolution requires either a verified AGI counterexample or an impossibility result. That is fair.

evidence.note: The original Transformer paper covers sequence modeling. It settles nothing about AGI.
ARC Prize, September 2026: Astra makes strong ARC-AGI-3 progress, but ARC declines to call it AGI. This does not meet the counterexample condition.
The AGI Society, September 2026, judges the published evidence insufficient to conclude Astra is AGI. That is not a proof of impossibility.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. By the evaluation date the packet shows no independently verified AGI built from attention-based LLMs alone, and no general impossibility result. Neither early-resolution condition is met, so the forecast cannot yet be scored.

attribution.note: It follows a mention of Steve Hsu's summary, but the first person ('In 1998 I wrote', 'Achilles' Heel I identified') marks the words as Marcus's own, and he endorses them.

semantics.note: Keeps the claim that the ASU study showed the weakness in 'the latest, greatest models', and treats 'every gadget' as rhetoric. This is an observation about what the study demonstrated.

contract.note: Judging what the pre-post study actually tested is a direct reading of the words 'The ASU team showed ... latest, greatest models'. That is fair.

evidence.note: The August 5 version trains small GPT-2-style models from scratch (4 layers, hidden size 32). The authors only assert that the findings extend to large models; they do not test contemporary leading models.

reviews.rationale: The contract's contradiction condition is met. The study used a materially different class of model, small models trained from scratch, and only asserted that its results apply to large pretrained models. It did not show the weakness in the latest, greatest models, as Marcus said it did.
